key_highlights: Iron ore crash confirmed, pressuring BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX and ASX200 Materials index
ASX edged higher on the day but 'stock shock' narrative building amid Fed meeting focus
Fuel price blowout intensifies political pressure for second excise cut, hitting energy and consumer sectors
Oil spike pressures Qantas (QAN.AX) and transport costs across the economy
Gold and critical-minerals juniors (Forrestania, PLC Resources, Critica, Sarytogan) attract capital rotation
Major private hospital operator breakup signals healthcare sector consolidation
ANZ.AX announces 3,500 job cuts; superannuation system under structural critique
Housing market softens further — no spring bounce in auctions, falling prices noted
Nvidia 2GW Australia AI data-centre push signals long-term tech infrastructure demand
China geopolitical pivot toward Trump regime adds commodity and trade-flow uncertainty

sectors.trend: Iron ore crash is the dominant negative; however, gold (Forrestania 2Mt WA deal, PLC Resources WA target) and critical minerals (Critica 19Mt tin-tungsten, Sarytogan 97.7% battery-grade graphite) draw rotation from large-cap iron ore names.
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face margin compression; junior gold and critical-minerals explorers (FOR.AX, PLC.AX, CTA.AX, SRY.AX) benefit from diversification flows. China demand pivot (#39) adds downside risk to iron ore.

sectors.trend: Fuel price blowout and oil spike raise input costs; Australia nears an energy inflection point (#29). Mongolian gas surge (#4) and shipping fuel-efficiency moves (#3) signal structural supply shifts.
sectors.implications: Woodside (WDS.AX), Santos (STO.AX) benefit from gas demand; QAN.AX and consumer staples face margin pressure from elevated fuel costs. Excise-cut debate adds policy uncertainty.

sectors.trend: ANZ.AX cuts 3,500 jobs in restructuring; superannuation system faces structural critique (#70). Migration policy overhaul (#34, #40) affects household credit demand.
sectors.implications: Big Four banks (CBA.AX, ANZ.AX, NAB.AX, WBC.AX) face cost-cutting narratives but stable NIMs. Super fund managers (HUB.AX, PPT.AX) under scrutiny. Housing softness (#46, #67) pressures mortgage growth.

sectors.trend: Major private hospital operator breakup via lender-backed consortium bid signals sector consolidation; J&J in talks to sell orthopaedics to Apollo for $20B globally.
sectors.implications: Adelaide Health (ADH.AX) and similar operators face M&A risk/opportunity. CSL.AX remains defensive anchor. Global pharma restructuring may affect Australian supply chains.

sectors.trend: No spring bounce in auction market; house prices falling; young homeowners accepting lower valuations. WA public housing failures noted.
sectors.implications: Property REITs (GPW.AX, DGL.AX) face occupancy and cap-rate pressure. Construction and building-product names under stress. Defensive rotation into infrastructure REITs likely.

sectors.trend: Nvidia 2GW Australia AI data-centre push; global AI capex debate (AMD, UiPath, Salesforce, Palo Alto). Trump's AI stance adds policy volatility.
sectors.implications: Australian data-centre and power-utility names (WEM.AX, CGP.AX) benefit from AI infrastructure build-out. Global tech valuations stretched; caution on high-multiple names.

key_themes: Iron ore demand shock and China trade-policy pivot
Energy transition inflection: gas, renewables, critical minerals
Housing market correction and REIT stress
Migration policy overhaul and productivity debate
Fed meeting and global rate-path uncertainty

risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce exposure to BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX; rotate into gold and critical-minerals juniors; hedge with commodity futures.

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Oil/fuel price spike and consumer inflation
risk_assessment.mitigation: Overweight energy producers (WDS.AX, STO.AX); underweight fuel-sensitive consumer names (QAN.AX, WES.AX). Monitor RBA response.
Underweight property REITs and construction; favour infrastructure and healthcare REITs. Monitor auction clearance rates.
Diversify away from China-exposed commodity names; monitor AUD/USD and iron ore contract prices weekly.

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Migration policy overhaul and productivity gap
risk_assessment.mitigation: Monitor labour-supply data; favour automation/tech beneficiaries over labour-intensive sectors.

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Fed meeting and global rate uncertainty
risk_assessment.mitigation: Maintain liquidity; avoid over-leveraged positions ahead of Fed decision. Watch AUD/USD for carry-trade unwind risk.

opportunities.recommendation: Rotate from large-cap iron ore into gold and critical-minerals juniors
opportunities.rationale: Iron ore crash diverts capital; Forrestania, PLC Resources, Critica, Sarytogan offer asymmetric upside in gold and battery materials.

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight Australian gas and energy producers
opportunities.rationale: Energy inflection point, Mongolian gas surge, and fuel-price blowout support domestic gas demand and pricing.

opportunities.recommendation: Position for AI data-centre build-out beneficiaries
opportunities.rationale: Nvidia 2GW Australia push drives power, cooling, and infrastructure demand over 3–5 years.
Private hospital operator breakup and global pharma restructuring create consolidation opportunities.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce or hedge large-cap iron ore exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: Confirmed iron ore crash and China demand pivot create sustained downside for BHP, RIO, FMG.
No auction bounce, falling house prices, and WA housing failures signal prolonged softness.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Maintain cash buffer ahead of Fed meeting
defensive_moves.rationale: Stock-shock narrative building; Fed decision and AUD/USD volatility warrant liquidity.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hedge fuel-cost inflation in consumer and transport
defensive_moves.rationale: Fuel blowout and oil spike compress margins for airlines and retailers.

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to remain range-bound to slightly lower over 1–3 months. Iron ore crash and oil spike create headwinds for Materials and Consumer; Fed meeting adds volatility. Gold and energy provide partial offset. Sentiment fragile — 'stock shock' narrative risks a sharper correction if commodity prices accelerate lower.
market_outlook.long_term: 6–12 month outlook cautiously constructive if iron ore stabilises and energy transition capex accelerates. AI infrastructure build-out, critical-minerals demand, and healthcare consolidation offer structural growth. Housing correction may deepen before stabilising. Migration policy overhaul could support medium-term labour supply but adds near-term uncertainty.
